title: Frequency response: filters, resonance and the Bode plot
goal: Measure the cutoff of an RC low-pass filter and the resonance and Q of a series RLC band-pass, by hand and with the Bode analyser.
theory: An RC low-pass passes low frequencies and attenuates high ones: |H| = 1/√(1 + (f/f_c)²), with f_c = 1/(2πRC) where the output is 3 dB down (70.7 %) and lags the input by 45°. Swapping R and C makes a high-pass with the same f_c.

A series RLC with the output across R is a band-pass: at f₀ = 1/(2π√(LC)) the inductor's and capacitor's reactances cancel and the gain peaks. The bandwidth between the −3 dB points is f₀/Q, with Q = (1/R)·√(L/C).
A Bode plot shows gain in dB (20·log₁₀|H|) and phase against frequency on a log axis. The Bode analyser sweeps the generator and plots both for you.
procedure: Load the reference build: generator → R1 → C1 (low-pass, output at column 16) and generator → L1 → C2 → R2 (band-pass, output at column 28).
By hand: set the generator to 1 Vpp sine, read the CH2/CH1 amplitude ratio at several frequencies and find where it falls to 0.707.
Open the Bode analyser: input = column 10, output = column 16, sweep 10 Hz–100 kHz. Record the −3 dB frequency.
Change the output to column 28 and record the resonance f₀ and Q.
